description: This topic deals with the study of chemical reactions occurring in the environment, the nature of pollutants, and their harmful effects on the ecosystem. It is a crucial segment of General Science for competitive exams.

sections.title: Air Pollution and Acid Rain
sections.description: Study of the degradation of air quality due to the introduction of harmful gases and particulate matter into the atmosphere.

key_concepts.explanation: Pollutants that are emitted directly from a source into the atmosphere (e.g., Carbon Monoxide - CO, Sulfur Dioxide - SO2, Nitrogen Oxides - NOx).
Pollutants that are not directly emitted but form when primary pollutants react in the atmosphere (e.g., Ozone - O3, PAN - Peroxyacetyl Nitrate).
A mixture of smoke and fog. Photochemical smog is formed by the reaction of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the presence of sunlight.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: SO2 + H2O → H2SO3 (Sulfurous Acid) and NO2 + H2O → HNO3 (Nitric Acid)
scientific_principles.application: Lowers the pH of rainwater below 5.6, causing damage to aquatic life and historical monuments like the Taj Mahal (a phenomenon known as 'Marble Cancer').

important_facts.fact: Carbon Monoxide (CO) combines with hemoglobin in the blood to form Carboxyhemoglobin, which is highly stable and severely inhibits oxygen transport.

sections.title: Global Warming and Ozone Depletion
sections.description: The rise in Earth's temperature due to greenhouse gases and the destruction of the protective ozone layer.

key_concepts.explanation: The process by which radiation from a planet's atmosphere warms the planet's surface to a temperature above what it would be without its atmosphere.

The thinning of the ozone (O3) layer in the stratosphere, primarily caused by the release of chemical compounds containing gaseous chlorine or bromine from industry and other human activities (like CFCs).

historical_events.significance: An international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances that are responsible for ozone depletion.
An international binding agreement committing its parties to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, based on the scientific consensus that global warming is occurring.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Approximately 10 to 50 km above Earth's surface
geographical_data.key_characteristics: The region of the atmosphere that contains the Ozone Layer, which absorbs the majority of the sun's harmful Ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

important_facts.fact: The major greenhouse gases in order of their contribution to the greenhouse effect: Water Vapor (H2O) > Carbon Dioxide (CO2) > Methane (CH4) > Nitrous Oxide (N2O).
The thickness of the ozone layer is measured in Dobson Units (DU).

sections.title: Water Pollution and Related Diseases
sections.description: Contamination of water bodies and the diseases caused by heavy metal toxicity.

key_concepts.explanation: The amount of dissolved oxygen needed by aerobic biological organisms to break down organic material present in a given water sample. High BOD indicates high water pollution.

The excessive richness of nutrients (especially nitrogen and phosphorus) in a lake or other body of water, frequently due to runoff from the land, which causes a dense growth of plant life and death of animal life from lack of oxygen.
The increasing concentration of a toxic substance (like pesticides or heavy metals) in the tissues of tolerant organisms at successively higher trophic levels in a food chain.

key_associations.extra_info: A severe neurological syndrome caused by severe mercury poisoning, often from eating contaminated fish.
Characterized by severe pain in the bones and joints, along with softening of the bones and kidney failure.
Decreases the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood in infants, causing their skin to turn blue.
Excess intake leads to severe dental and skeletal degradation.

sections.title: Environmental Protection: Laws and Policies
sections.description: Legal, constitutional, and social measures taken in India to protect the environment and control pollution.

polity_articles.provision: The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country.
polity_articles.details: Added to the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

polity_articles.provision: It shall be the fundamental duty of every citizen of India to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life.
polity_articles.details: Added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee as a Fundamental Duty.

historical_events.significance: Enacted to ensure the protection of plant and animal species and prevent illegal poaching and smuggling of wildlife.

historical_events.event: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
historical_events.significance: Enacted to prevent water pollution and established the Central and State Pollution Control Boards (CPCB and SPCB).
Enacted in the wake of the 1984 Bhopal Gas Tragedy. It acts as an 'umbrella legislation' designed to provide a framework for central government coordination of environmental activities.

key_associations.extra_info: A non-violent, forest conservation movement in Uttarakhand aimed at preventing deforestation by hugging trees.
A powerful social movement consisting of adivasis, farmers, and environmentalists against the construction of large dams across the Narmada River.
